findings.title: Scope and mechanism match the slice plan entry with correct layering
findings.description: Every element the plan's 915 entry assigns appears in Technical Scope: the `scope` field on `CONFIG_KEYS` (`packages/core/src/config/ConfigKeys.ts` — confirmed the interface exists there today without it), project-file routing through `ConfigManager`/`configPaths.ts` (confirmed current `getProjectConfigPath`-based routing in `ConfigManager.ts:129/179/198`), the minimal one-line gitignore addition (matching the plan's "not a full gitignore overhaul, tracked separately as Future Work"), and a migration story for pre-existing committed personal keys. The routing-inside-`ConfigManager` decision keeps all listed callers unchanged, and MCP `configTools.ts` (which imports `getProjectConfigPath` directly, confirmed at `configTools.ts:3,40`) is the only MCP touchpoint — matching the plan's note that this slice "touches packages/mcp-server config tools too." No scope creep detected; exclusions (auto-fix wiring, gitignore overhaul, CLI surface changes) are deliberate and justified against the existing closed `fixAction` union (confirmed in `ConsistencyChecker.ts:206-220`).

findings.title: Failure modes for new I/O paths are enumerated with explicit strategies
findings.description: The design covers the three new I/O surfaces: `migrate-personal`'s two-file rewrite (write-personal-then-delete-shared ordering, per-key failure isolation with `failed: <error>` reporting, idempotent re-runs, partial-failure leaves the key in both files rather than neither), writes to `.context-forge.local.toml` (same `writeToml` helper and throw-on-failure contract as existing files — verified accurate against `ConfigManager.ts:33-39`), and the `cf init` gitignore append (permission failure throws through the existing `handleError` path — verified `init.ts` has that top-level handler). No network/subprocess I/O is introduced, so hang/timeout classes don't apply here; the local-file failure classes are handled. No "TBD" remaining.

findings.title: Delete routing cannot clear a stale shared-file copy, contradicting the design's own collision remediation and walkthrough step 9
findings.description: The Delete rule states delete "mirrors write — deletes from whichever project file the key's scope maps to." For a personal key (`git.integration_branch`), that is `.context-forge.local.toml` only. But the collision semantics (line 146) instruct the user to clear a skipped stale shared-file copy via "a separate, explicit `cf config unset <key> --project`", and Verification Walkthrough step 9 (line 259) relies on exactly that command to make `cf check` clean again. Under the design's own routing, `cf config unset git.integration_branch --project` deletes from the **personal** file — destroying the developer's local value the collision rule just protected — while the stale shared copy survives, so the `personal-config-in-shared-file` finding persists and step 9's expected outcomes fail on both counts. The design provides no user-facing path that removes a personal-scope key from the *shared* file outside `migrate-personal`'s happy path, yet the skip-case remediation and the "cf check is clean again" success expectation depend on one. The requirement left unmet is the plan's "defined migration/compat story": the collision branch of that story is not actually executable as specified. Fix in design before task breakdown — e.g. personal-key `unset --project` clears both project files, or `migrate-personal` gains an explicit overwrite/clear action for the skipped case — and update lines 146 and 259 to match.

findings.title: Design declares a dependency the slice plan entry does not
findings.description: Frontmatter and Prerequisites declare `dependencies: [914]`, while the 900 slice plan's 915 entry says "Dependencies: none." This is a benign refinement, not a contradiction: the design classifies `git.integration_branch`, which only exists under that name because of 914, and 914 is already marked complete in the plan. Worth a one-line sync in the plan entry (or a note in the design explaining the delta) so the artifact trail stays consistent, but no action blocking.

findings.title: `cf init` gitignore insertion point is unspecified, though the walkthrough requires it in the `--lite` path
findings.description: The component structure lists `init.ts` but not where in `cf init`'s flow the gitignore line lands. Current `init.ts` skips guides/commands/IDE steps under `--lite`, and the Verification Walkthrough (steps 1 and 3) runs `cf init --lite` and then expects `.gitignore` to contain the line — so the addition must sit outside the `if (!opts.lite)` block, alongside project registration. The walkthrough would catch a wrong placement during implementation, but stating the placement (and that it applies in lite mode) would remove the ambiguity cheaply.
